--- title: "Listening comprehension (uncued)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_SEM_COMPRENSION_NCP" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (G · Comprehension; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_SEM_COMPRENSION_NCP`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Comprensión oral (sin pistas)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_SEM_COMPRENSION_NCP.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Listening comprehension (uncued), at age 6 (1,697 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .55 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 91 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 10 | | Task family | G · Comprehension | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | Questions based on the text content. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_decision.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **receptive oral language**. In listening comprehension, the child hears a text without seeing it and answers questions by choosing among options. In multiple-choice vocabulary, the child hears a word and chooses among four pictures. In the simple view of reading, listening comprehension is the component that does not depend on reading [@hoover1990simple]. The vocabulary framework covers expressive and reading vocabulary. **What the evidence says:** - **In transparent orthographies, listening comprehension is the best predictor of reading comprehension.** In 1,895 Italian children from Grade 1 to Grade 5, listening comprehension predicted reading comprehension in every grade and reading accuracy played a smaller role [@tobia2015simple]. In 1,815 Finnish children, the effect of fluency disappeared after Grade 1 and that of listening comprehension remained until Grade 3 [@torppa2016simple]. In 4,750 Dominican schoolchildren, its weight grows as reading comprehension improves [@sanchezvincitore2022svr]. - **Preschool oral language anticipates reading comprehension.** In children aged 4 to 6, inferences, literal comprehension of a story and grammar predicted reading comprehension a year later; vocabulary acted through them [@silva2014comprehension]. Language in a broad sense predicts more than vocabulary alone [@lervag2018comprehension]. - **Receptive vocabulary predicts level, not rate.** In two Australian samples (N = 4,983 and 4,570), receptive vocabulary at age 4 predicted comprehension at age 8, but its growth was not related to reading growth between ages 8 and 14 [@larsen2026receptive]. The relation is weak in the first grades, when decoding limits comprehension, and grows later. These tasks can be expected to predict little in the short term. **What our data show.** They are the weakest tasks in their domain: - **Low consistency.** Listening comprehension has α = .30 with 10 items; multiple-choice vocabulary, α = .51. The latter is also very unstable across terms (ρ = .12–.14) and its observed maximum (25) exceeds the number of items (17), which needs to be reviewed. - **Low predictive validity.** Against low reading comprehension at ages 7 and 8, the AUC is .58–.59 for listening comprehension and .52–.58 for vocabulary. They are not suitable for individual decisions. Before using them in articles, the items and scoring should be reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 919| 263| 655| 34| | 6.1| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 778| 0| 778| 31| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 7.38| 1.43| 7| -0.73| 0.38| 4.94| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–10 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range |Warning | |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|:--------------------| | 6.1| 263|4–10 |0–10 |0–10 |extreme value: check | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .30. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (6.1, r = .23). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .55. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.59. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_COMPRENSION_NCP_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .54 (1 time point; 511–511 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 5| 6| 6| 7| 7| 8| 9| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_COMPRENSION_NCP_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,684| 0.035| 0.152| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,692| -0.030| 0.536| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,687| 0.022| 0.367| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,697| 0.025| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Listening comprehension (uncued)” (code 91; LEEDUCA battery) assesses listening comprehension. The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 10 items. The time limit is 150 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 and 2011 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .30 (N = 1,699, 10 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.59. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 6.1: the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
